leaseLedger.integrity: Every record contains a deterministic SHA-256 recordHash.
leaseLedger.allocation: Exclusive claim filenames allocate monotonically increasing integer fencing tokens. Invalid or abandoned claim filenames burn tokens but cannot activate.
leaseLedger.election: The lowest live cooperative contender activates. Inspection treats the highest active fencing token as authoritative if contradictory active records exist.
leaseLedger.expiry: Latest valid activation or heartbeat expiresAtMs controls active ownership.
leaseLedger.release: Release is append-only and scoped to fencing token plus lease ID.

operationalProjection: scheduler job identity, status, base revision and queued handoff identities
deferred mailbox ownership, identities, retries and expiry epochs
pending compaction IDs, generations, stages and before/after hashes
cell wake state, activation count and latest wake/sleep event IDs
checkpointAdmission.payloadBoundary: The full serialized world remains separately protected by payloadHash. operationalHash is a selected coordination witness, not a duplicate full-payload hash.

fencing.staleHandle: A lease handle fails after a higher active fencing token takes over.
fencing.staleBase: A leased checkpoint fails when the durable generation/snapshot ID differs from the lease base.
fencing.transientPolicy: Lower-token leased temp and recoveryTemp candidates are ineligible for a higher-token writer.
fencing.committedHistory: Primary and backup candidates are not rejected merely because their committed checkpoint token is older.
fencing.baseCheck: Immediately before primary rename, the installed primary generation and snapshot ID are compared with the admitted base.

verifiedTests: one active writer lease blocks a second cooperative writer
simultaneous cooperative claims elect exactly one active writer
release permits immediate acquisition with a strictly higher fencing token
heartbeat renewal extends ownership and later stale takeover fences the old writer
an invalid burned claim cannot become active and the next token remains monotonic
leased checkpoint embeds fencing evidence and advances the lease base
a stale checkpoint base is rejected even while the same lease remains current
a stale owner cannot checkpoint after a higher fencing token takes over
checkpoint barrier rejects an unquiesced receiving cell
checkpoint operational hash covers pending queues, mailboxes, and compaction journals
checkpoint tampering invalidates the deterministic snapshot identity
new fencing token discards an older leased temp that never reached primary commit
lease expiry during save prevents primary installation and the next owner fences the temp
leased checkpoint refuses a durable base changed by a non-cooperating writer
stale-owner recovery succeeds after process exit at AFTER_CLAIM_FSYNC
stale-owner recovery succeeds after process exit at AFTER_ACTIVATION_FSYNC
stale-owner recovery succeeds after process exit at AFTER_BASE_RECORD_FSYNC
process exit after durable release permits immediate replacement

processExit.method: Child Node.js process calls process.exit(86) after a durable lease stage; a later writer attempts acquisition.
processExit.result: All four lease process-exit tests passed under their tested expiry or release condition.

authorityBoundary.statement: Writer coordination may admit or reject a checkpoint but does not define canonical physical rules. Lease, fence and checkpoint fields are excluded from canonical physical truth.

claimBoundary: The protocol fences cooperating writers that use the lease and leased-checkpoint APIs; it is not hostile raw-filesystem writer enforcement.
Lease expiry uses supplied millisecond time. Cross-machine clock skew, clock rollback, VM suspension and distributed consensus are not solved.
There is a narrow interval between the final pre-rename assertion and rename; no kernel-enforced compare-and-swap currently closes it.
The checkpoint operational hash covers selected coordination projections, while payloadHash protects the complete world.
The lease ledger is append-only and has no verified garbage-collection or archival protocol.
Legacy uncheckpointed v0.01 transients contain no fencing token and are not retroactively classified as stale leased candidates.
Immediate parent/base evidence is verified; complete snapshot and fencing lineage is not.
The checkpoint API does not freeze arbitrary caller mutation throughout the asynchronous save.
Process-exit evidence is not universal sudden-power-loss evidence.
No production-scale, massive-world, multiplayer or AI claim is established.
